compiled_state.description:
# Generic, config-driven status-map override seam

## Problem / findings

An audit of the Jira reconciler bridge surfaced a live-workflow change: the REB
Jira project now has a valid **Blocked** status. Absorbing that today would
require editing core rebar's hardcoded status maps, which is an anti-pattern —
core rebar must stay project-agnostic; a single project's workflow states must
never be named in shipped code.

### Current state of status mapping (as found)

Status mapping is HARDCODED in three places, with no config-driven seam:

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py`
  — `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` (outbound), `blocked -> "In Progress"`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py`
  — `local_to_jira_status` (outbound, blocked -> In Progress) and
    `jira_to_local_status` (inbound, already has `"Blocked": "blocked"`).
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py`
  — `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` (inbound, already has `"Blocked": "blocked"`) plus
    `_REBAR_STATUS_LABEL_TO_LOCAL` label precedence.

Consequences observed:

- `blocked` and `in_progress` BOTH map outbound to Jira "In Progress"
  (non-injective forward map); `blocked` only round-trips via the
  `rebar-status:blocked` annotation label.
- The ONLY external control today is the `REBAR_RECONCILER_STATUS_GATING` env
  gate — not a per-project mapping. `rebar.toml`'s `[reconciler]` section has
  adapter/code-health keys but nothing for status mapping.
- The inbound direction already accepts `"Blocked" -> blocked`; the outbound
  direction still downgrades `blocked -> "In Progress"`.

## Intent

Introduce a ONE-TIME, generic, provider-neutral, project-agnostic
**status-map override** seam read from project configuration (e.g. a
`[reconciler.status_map]` table in `rebar.toml`), with the current hardcoded
maps as the DEFAULT fallback. After this seam exists:

- The REB "Blocked" change — and any future per-project workflow variance — is
  expressed purely as project config data, never as a core edit.
- Portability falls out for free: only a project that declares an override gets
  it; projects whose workflow lacks a Blocked state keep today's behavior with
  zero changes. No project-specific capability gating is added to core.

## Scope / non-goals

- IN scope: generic config-override machinery (parse, validate, merge over
  defaults for both inbound and outbound directions), default-preserving
  behavior, round-trip / parity test coverage, docs (`docs/config.md`,
  reconciler mapping docs), and the `project.portability` plan-review
  criterion.
- OUT of scope: naming any specific project's states in core; changing the
  default maps; the REB project's own `rebar.toml` values (that is downstream
  project config once the seam lands).

## Notes

- Illegal-transition handling already exists at
  `dispatch_one.py:402,445`; the override must interoperate with it.
- Parity between the map copies is currently enforced by
  `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_config.py` — the seam must keep a single
  source of truth or keep that parity green.

**This epic is filed for future work and is intentionally out of scope for the
current session (no implementation here).**
compiled_state.title: Generic config-driven status-map override seam for per-project Jira workflow variance
